bug_semantics: The email-verification trust boundary was client-controlled in two complementary ways. The verification feature added is_email_verified and verified_at to profile while the existing authenticated profile UPDATE policy restricted only rows, not columns, so an authenticated user could PATCH their own /rest/v1/profile row and set is_email_verified=true. It also put {profileId, orgSiteName} into unsigned Base64 and /api/verify decoded that attacker-malleable data and set the named profile verified without integrity, ownership, or expiry checks. A later member of the same squashed feature made that handler use the Supabase service-role client, bypassing RLS and making a forged profileId capable of targeting an arbitrary profile.
flaw_origin: Original email-verification implementation on the retained origin/email-verification feature branch, not a move or refactor. Commit 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf first added the verification columns, the unsigned Base64 link generator, and the trusting /api/verify update handler; commit 947cfc06ca3a858972e8faafd096c7f662ef6086 in the same squash series later amplified the handler to a service-role arbitrary-profile update. Mainline commit bd905b580a203309e244db16b06187c5103924cc is the squash aggregate and is therefore not used as the BIC.
ai_marker: Absent. `git cat-file -p 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf` contains author and committer `emmanuel <chifez1@gmail.com>` and only the message `worked on the email verification`; it has no Co-authored-by/Generated-with trailer, AI identity, or bot identity.
evidence: Disclosure and attack path: https://gist.github.com/prashunbaral/70c4f6f9d9ff8b82295623073eb41f3a describes authenticated manipulation of is_email_verified through /rest/v1/profile and forging Base64 JSON for GET /api/verify?data=...; GHSA-j8cg-23h3-5p99 identifies affected versions before v0.2.6 and the v0.2.6 release.

Smallest source commit: `git show 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf -- supabase/migrations/20240320081809_email_verification.sql apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/email/verify_email/+server.js apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/verify/+server.js` shows one commit newly adding the two profile verification columns, JSON.stringify({profileId, orgSiteName}) followed by btoa, and a GET handler that atob/JSON.parse's client data and updates is_email_verified=true by profileId. `git grep -n -F 'Users can update own profile' 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf -- supabase` shows the extant row-only policy `USING (auth.uid() = id)`, which did not prohibit updating the newly added verification column.

Direct parent absence: `git cat-file -p 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf` gives sole parent 62a32a62046302c6247b863f9f39cd610125c083. `git grep -n -E 'is_email_verified|/api/verify|verificationData' 62a32a62046302c6247b863f9f39cd610125c083 -- apps/dashboard supabase` returns no matches; both endpoint files and the verification-column migration are additions in 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf.

Squash decomposition: `git merge-base origin/email-verification bd905b580a203309e244db16b06187c5103924cc^` is 62a32a62046302c6247b863f9f39cd610125c083. `git log --reverse 62a32a62046302c6247b863f9f39cd610125c083..origin/email-verification` yields the seven non-merge member commits listed in decomposed_shas (plus merge-only 6da395eadf17063ca2bf0e065efbac3676a46735). The bd905b580a203309e244db16b06187c5103924cc message repeats those seven member subjects. `git diff --exit-code dd71b639355ad09aa02b225e2e126975261962fa bd905b580a203309e244db16b06187c5103924cc --` over the two endpoint files, migration, and supabase.server.ts exits zero, proving the retained branch's relevant tip content is what the squash landed. Mainline `git log -L 7,21:apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/verify/+server.js 43e6cd611db5a666d8a0a8a493222ef5f61d56f1` consequently stops at squash aggregate bd905b580a203309e244db16b06187c5103924cc; decomposition recovers 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf as the first writer.

Lifecycle activation and persistence: `git show 947cfc06ca3a858972e8faafd096c7f662ef6086 -- apps/dashboard/src/lib/utils/functions/supabase.server.ts apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/verify/+server.js` changes the already unsigned handler from an anonymous client to PRIVATE_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE and retains the unvalidated profileId update, making arbitrary-profile forged links effective. `git log --all -S'btoa(verificationData)' --` traces the vulnerable expression from 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf through squash/refactor history until removal by the fix; 5cb6f475110c97c77090966a8891fdec70712d30, a8ce996e021a71cc8214c0b5be6d7b9f4172161e, and b96d91cd7c25e64db46e12e11a8ca7450c9f2538 only adjust SvelteKit redirect syntax, rename JS/TS, or reformat the link and do not introduce the flaw.

Version boundary: mainline squash bd905b580a203309e244db16b06187c5103924cc is absent from v0.1.1 and contained by v0.1.2 onward; `git diff --name-status v0.1.1^{commit} v0.1.2^{commit} --` for the verify handler and verification migration reports both as added. The last advisory-affected release is v0.2.5 (peeled commit 900f5ec12979f512ae8f333312aee78973a054f5). `git for-each-ref` shows annotated tag v0.2.6 peels to 25d1a8d710fed1a4de98f02f1bcfdf215c149be5, matching the vendor's security release at https://github.com/classroomio/classroomio/releases/tag/v0.2.6.

Closing fix: `git show 25d1a8d710fed1a4de98f02f1bcfdf215c149be5 -- apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/email/verify_email/+server.ts apps/dashboard/src/routes/api/verify/+server.js supabase/migrations/20241203000001_email_verification_security.sql` removes Base64 JSON and the direct profileId update, generates a random stored one-hour token bound to profile/email, validates existence/use/expiry/current email, and adds a trigger rejecting direct is_email_verified/verified_at changes outside the secure verification context. The commit's sole parent is 43e6cd611db5a666d8a0a8a493222ef5f61d56f1 and its message explicitly names both client-side status manipulation and Base64 token forgery, so the same commit is both the direct code fix and the v0.2.6 release commit.

BIC-only AI check: the raw commit object for 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf names human author/committer emmanuel <chifez1@gmail.com> and has no AI/bot marker or trailer. No PR text, squash message, later refactor, or fix metadata was used for the AI judgment.
reasoning: The first vulnerable observable state appears in the retained feature-branch commit 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf: it creates a verification flag that ordinary authenticated profile updates can set and implements verification data as unsigned Base64. Its direct parent has none of the feature. Although 947cfc06ca3a858972e8faafd096c7f662ef6086 later increases the unsigned endpoint's impact by using service-role credentials, it is not the first vulnerability because the direct profile-field bypass already exists after 69ba4c1a23504004f9d888312916862fb93003bf. The public retained feature branch permits decomposing mainline squash bd905b580a203309e244db16b06187c5103924cc rather than mislabeling that aggregate as the BIC. Release commit 25d1a8d710fed1a4de98f02f1bcfdf215c149be5 closes both paths in v0.2.6. Because the BIC commit object has no AI or bot signal, the protocol requires NOT_AI.
